source.check: Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), no poll in this division; read from the INA page OCR, where the surname and other-names columns are separate runs aligned here by row order (INA page images need a subscription). The member is a retiring member (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5, names the only four new members) who is not the 1946 member, so he came in between 1946 and 1949; the Council meeting of 9 June 1952 names him (Ulster Herald, 14 June 1952, p. 2)

note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Omagh rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. For the first time in 25 years four divisions were contested (Bencran, Gortin, Maine, Moyle), three by Anti-Partitionists and one by an Independent, all against Unionists. 'Seventeen Unionists and seventeen Anti-Partitionists were returned unopposed, but in one Nationalist division no nomination was received and the retiring member will be deemed re-elected'; four new members came in unopposed (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5). The unopposed members are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), read from the page OCR. Tattymoyle has no candidate in the notice's name columns; it is evidently the Nationalist division where the retiring member was deemed re-elected, but no source read names him, so it is not recorded. Not the member returned in 1946 (Francis Crane); the change is not explained in the sources read. 'Mr. Crozier Beatty' (C. S. Beattie) is a member in June 1952. Returned unopposed.
